title: A lisse E sheaf has a constructible integral lattice
statement: Use the coefficient conventions of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and schemes of [def-pc-scheme]. Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Here noetherian means that $T$ has a finite affine cover by spectra of noetherian rings, finite-dimensional means a finite bound on the lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets, and invertible means that $\ell\cdot1$ is a unit in each local ring. On $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] write $E_T(V)=C(|V|,E)$ and $A_T(V)=C(|V|,A)$ for the sheaves of continuous functions with pointwise ring operations and restriction by precomposition, so $A_T$ is the completed coefficient sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $L$ be an $E_T$-module sheaf which is pro-etale locally free of finite rank. There is an $A_T$-module sheaf $N$, and an isomorphism $E_T\otimes_{A_T}N\cong L$, such that $N$ admits a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] on every stratum of which it is pro-etale locally $A_T\otimes_A P$ for a finitely presented $A$-module $P$. The tensor product is the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The assertion requires only a constructible integral sheaf; it does not require $N$ to be locally free on all of $T$.

proof.text: Write $S(M)=E_T\otimes_{A_T}M$. The coefficient theorem gives $E_T=A_T[1/\varpi]$. The fraction relation expresses $S$ as the sequential colimit of multiplication by $\varpi$; the two colimit nodes make it exact. For constructible integral $P,Q$, the integral characterization puts $P[0]$ in the bounded constructible complete category. The Hom-sum lemma verifies the countable bounded-below Hom hypothesis of the scalar-localization theorem. Apply the latter with $K=P[0],L=Q[0],q=1$ and [def-pc-ext]. It yields $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{A_T}(P,Q)[1/\varpi]\cong\operatorname{Ext}^1_{E_T}(SP,SQ)$, with $\alpha/\varpi^m\mapsto\varpi^{-m}S\alpha$. Thus the integral extension criterion applies to every such pair on $T$ and on its noetherian finite-dimensional locally closed subschemes with $\ell$ invertible.

source.place: Lemmas 6.8.12 and 6.8.13, Ext formula in the last paragraph

proof.text: Use the closed-subsets-minimal theorem to induct over reduced induced closed subschemes $X\subseteq T$, for every lisse rational sheaf on each $X$. Such $X$ is noetherian (ideal chains in an affine quotient lift to ideal chains upstairs), finite-dimensional (closed irreducible chains remain chains in $T$), and $\ell$-coprime (an inverse maps to an inverse). Empty support has the zero model. For nonempty $X$, the reduced-open lemma gives a nonempty quasi-compact open $U$ with a lisse integral model $M_U$. The reduced induced closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ has strictly smaller support. The sheaf $i^{-1}L$ is lisse on $Z$: the inverse image of a pro-etale covering of $X$ trivializing $L$ is a pro-etale covering of $Z$, inverse image commutes with finite direct sums and with restriction to its members, and the coefficient theorem identifies $i^{-1}E_X$ with $E_Z$. So induction supplies a constructible integral model $M_Z$ of $i^{-1}L$, with $S_Z(M_Z)\cong i^{-1}L$. A lisse finite free model is constructible using the single stratum and its local free modules.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13, constructible filtration expressed by noetherian induction

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-model-open-closed-pieces] to $U,Z,M_U,M_Z$. It produces constructible integral sheaves $Q=j_!M_U$, $P=i_*M_Z$ and the exact sequence $0\to S_XQ\to L\to S_XP\to0$. Step 1 supplies the denominator hypothesis for this $P,Q$. [lem-weil-pbc-integral-models-extension-closed] gives a constructible integral $N_X$ with $S_XN_X\cong L$. This proves the induction step.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13, last paragraph: gluing the two pieces via extension classes

proof.text: Let $r:T_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow T$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme with full support. Inverse image preserves a finite free trivializing cover, and the coefficient theorem identifies its ring with $E_{T_{\mathrm{red}}}$; thus $r^{-1}L$ is lisse. Induction gives it a constructible integral model $M$. Apply the open-closed pieces lemma with closed part $r$, empty complementary open, and zero open model. It gives constructible $N=r_*M$ and $0\to0\to L\to S_TN\to0$, hence $S_TN\cong L$. This includes empty, rank-zero, disconnected and nonreduced cases.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13, reduction to full reduced support and final integral structure

lean.statement: theorem exists_constructible_integral_lattice (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian T] (_hdim : ∃ d : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim T ≤ d) (_hℓ : ∀ x : T, IsUnit (l : T.presheaf.stalk x)) (L : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (latticeModuleRing T (WithAbs (Padic.coefficientExtensionAbsoluteValue l E)))) [L.IsFiniteLocallyFree] : ∃ N : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (latticeModuleRing T (latticeCoefficientIntegers l E)), IsContinuousConstructible T (latticeCoefficientIntegers l E) N ∧ Nonempty (SheafOfModules.changeOfRings.{u, u + 1, u + 1} (integralLatticeCoefficientMap T l E) N ≅ L)
lean.note: Uses the canonical continuous coefficient sheaves and valuation topology of the landed lattice-coefficient interface. Constructibility is stratumwise, and no global locally-free hypothesis is imposed on N. Maintainer fix: IsNoetherian T bundles exactly the original locally-noetherian and compact hypotheses and supplies the topologically-noetherian instance for the source-scoped constructibility predicate.
